note: Three attempts to fix the abstention contract ('if no candidate shows it, answer none') all failed, and the frame-signal analysis explains why. Recorded so the next person does not repeat them.

problem.what: 4 of the 5 wrong photos in the English holdout are not mis-picks. They are guides where no candidate was usable and the model picked one anyway. Pure mis-picking among usable candidates happened once in 116 guides (0.9%).
cases: #11 PLGmTzEGSIY vg-2 (putty knife, workbench wide shot)
#22 wRAtVLgj-wU vg-1 (supine butterfly, room wide shot)
#50 tNxa0ngtQJw vg-1 (flattened clay bead, small subject on a mat)
#60 jJWl9Kpwbno vg-2 (wick trimmer, frame full of candles)

attempts.idea: Tighten the verification prompt (identifiability clause: 'too small or far to make out → false')
attempts.measured: Caught 0 of the 2 target cases; added 1 false rejection on the 34 human-judged frames.

attempts.idea: Self-consistency voting — ask verification 3x, require unanimous true
attempts.result: FAILED worse than the baseline it replaced
attempts.measured: Blocked 0 of 4 failures (all four returned [True, True, True]); discarded 24 of 32 human-approved frames. The model's instability is noise, not an uncertainty signal: it is confidently wrong on the failures and wobbles on the correct ones.

attempts.idea: Code-side frame statistics to detect wide shots (edge density, flat-area ratio, centre concentration, sharpness, contrast)
attempts.measured: All five signals put the 4 failures inside the 10-90 percentile band of the 32 good frames, and the failures disagree with each other: #50 is the flattest frame in the set (edge 4.6, flat 0.94) while #60 is the busiest (edge 23.7).

why_they_fail.common_shape: Every attempt either re-asks the same model that just got it wrong, or measures the image without knowing what the image is supposed to contain.
why_they_fail.the_wall: 'Does this frame contain what the guide asks for?' is a semantic judgement. When the model is confidently wrong about it, neither re-prompting nor pixel statistics recovers the right answer. #60 proves the point: the subject fills the frame, it is just the wrong subject — no measure of 'how big is the thing' can see that.
why_they_fail.not_one_phenomenon: These were grouped as 'wide shots' but they are not one failure. #50 fails because the subject is tiny; #60 fails because the frame is full of the wrong object.

what_actually_worked_instead: Removing the prompt cap on guide count (coverage 43% -> 73% on long videos, 41% -> 66% overall for short)
Targeted re-query of steps with no guide (honest coverage 38% -> 69%)
All three are deterministic or structural changes, not attempts to talk the model out of a mistake.
residual_risk_is_bounded: Wrong photos are 1-4% and the product already routes around them: auto-pick is off by default, and when on, the picker still opens for human review. A wrong photo cannot reach a document silently.
